pathway.title: PBF Holding Co LLC — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, the issuer's balance sheet is strong at the latest reported date. Principal debt was USD 1,850.0 million against cash of USD 2,510.6 million, giving net cash of USD 660.6 million and leverage of 0.5x total debt and -0.2x net debt on twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 3,505.2 million [CP-1 net debt and leverage calculation]. After the redemption of USD 800.0 million of 9.875% notes on 26 October 2026 for about USD 853.4 million, principal falls to USD 1,050.0 million and cash to roughly USD 1,657.2 million before accrued interest and other flows, which is an illustration and not a reported balance [CP-1 illustrative effects]. Category: Documentary Fact for the reported figures, Analyst Interpretation for the illustration.

Second, the issuer's earnings swung from a trough to very high levels, and the trailing figure is concentrated. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 29.5 million in FY2025, USD 1,139.3 million in Q2 2026 and USD 2,139.3 million in Q3 2026 [CP-1 financials table]. The business is priced at spot market and has no contractual margin protection, so the issuer's debt capacity follows crack spreads, crude differentials, throughput and compliance costs [CP-1A operating model]. Management attributes the 2026 strength to conflict-driven market conditions and describes them as uncertain in duration; that is Management Language and is not adopted as a forecast. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

Third, the issuer's refinancing in 2026 removed near-term maturities and lowered stated coupon cost. The 6.00% notes due 2028 and 7.875% notes due 2030 were redeemed, USD 500.0 million of 7.25% notes due 2034 and USD 550.0 million of zero-coupon exchangeable notes due 2032 were issued, and the secured revolver was extended with a USD 4,000.0 million commitment [CP-1A transaction summary]. Stated coupons retired of about USD 166.5 million a year compare with about USD 36.3 million on the new fixed notes, excluding revolver fees and discount amortisation. The exchangeable notes settle principal in cash and are linked to the parent's share price, creating a fair-value liability of USD 197.6 million that moves earnings [CP-1 debt instruments; CP-1A transaction summary]. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation.

Fourth, claims outside the reported debt are material. They include operating lease liabilities of USD 712.3 million at 30 September 2026, pension and post-retirement medical deficits of USD 89.8 million and USD 16.4 million at 31 December 2025, fixed purchase commitments of USD 642.9 million, renewable energy credit and emissions obligations of USD 486.5 million and environmental liabilities of USD 148.4 million, plus unquantified investigations into the Martinez fire and catalyst release [CP-1 claims outside the debt figure]. These rank alongside debt in a downside case and are not in the leverage ratios. Category: Documentary Fact.

Fifth, the issuer's cash flows with its parent were supportive in the downturn and have turned outward as earnings recovered. Parent contributions exceeded distributions by USD 199.6 million in FY2025, but in Q3 2026 distributions exceeded contributions by USD 60.9 million, and the issuer may distribute cash to fund the parent's dividend [CP-1A ownership and behaviour]. Documented behaviour toward creditors is Neutral or Mixed: full redemptions at par or a premium and transparent reporting are supportive, while past asset distributions to affiliates and the parent-level secured note on the hydrogen plants are open. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

Sixth, the evidence has gaps that limit how far the view can be pushed: no forecast or through-the-cycle earnings case, no executed indentures or credit agreement, a liquidity figure that cannot be rebuilt, and an unexplained difference between issuer and parent debt figures.

runs.text: Strengths. The issuer has low reported leverage and net cash: 0.5x total debt and -0.2x net debt to twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, and cash interest paid of USD 162.3 million against Adjusted EBITDA of USD 3,505.2 million, or 21.6x cover on a measure that excludes capitalised interest [CP-1 interest cover]. Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading. The issuer has liquidity depth, with USD 2,510.6 million of cash and about USD 3,100.0 million of rounded borrowing availability, and no revolver drawing at the quarter end [CP-1 liquidity]. Its maturity profile has no drawn debt maturing before 2032 after the October redemption [CP-1 debt maturities]. Its asset base is diversified across six refineries in four regions with one customer at about 13% of revenue, so customer loss is a smaller risk than a single refinery event [CP-1A operating model]. The parent supported the issuer with net contributions of USD 199.6 million in the FY2025 downturn and contributed the hydrogen plants in Q3 2026 [CP-1A ownership and behaviour].

Weaknesses. The issuer's earnings depend on external margins and uptime: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 29.5 million in FY2025 against USD 3,505.2 million over the latest twelve months, with USD 3,278.6 million from two quarters. Analyst Interpretation resting on the CP-1 figures. The issuer faces event risk at single sites: the Martinez fire investigations and the 8 May 2026 Chalmette fire have no quantified impact [CP-1A transaction summary]. Cash can leave to the parent chain and the exchangeable notes link the issuer to the parent's share price, with a fair-value liability of USD 197.6 million [CP-1A behaviour table; CP-1 debt instruments]. Large claims sit outside debt, notably leases, purchase commitments, emissions credits and environmental liabilities [CP-1 claims outside debt]. The revolver is secured and ranks ahead of the unsecured notes to the extent of its collateral; the unsecured notes are also structurally behind non-guarantor subsidiaries, a structural mechanic and not a recovery conclusion [CP-1 debt instruments]. Regulatory compliance cost is large and volatile: renewable fuel compliance cost was USD 522.8 million in Q3 2026 against USD 169.0 million a year earlier [CP-1A operating model].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: All items below are Documentary Facts from the issuer's filings unless marked, with their status. No transaction is a sponsor transaction: the context names no sponsor and the pack describes none.

2034 7.25% senior notes. Type: new senior unsecured notes. Parties: PBF Holding and PBF Finance as issuers with certain subsidiary guarantors, Wilmington Trust as trustee. Status: completed 2026-05-28 (Q3-10Q page:21 "the Issuers issued $500.0 million in aggregate principal amount of 2034 7.25% Senior Notes"). Use of proceeds: net proceeds of 492.1 plus available cash redeemed all of the 2028 6.00% notes on 2026-06-25 (Q3-10Q page:23 "On June 25, 2026, the Company redeemed all $801.6 million aggregate principal amount outstanding of its 2028 6.00% Senior Notes"). Terms: guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis, effectively subordinated to secured debt including the revolver, structurally subordinated to non-guarantor subsidiaries, with a change-of-control repurchase at 101% on a ratings decline (Q3-10Q page:23 "at a purchase price of 101% of the principal amount"). Liquidity effect: cash used was the shortfall between the notes redeemed and net proceeds, and the 2028 maturity was removed. Creditor implication: the nearest maturity moved from 2028 to 2034 for this tranche, at a higher coupon than the notes replaced but with maturity extension; Analyst Interpretation.

2032 0.00% exchangeable senior notes. Type: new senior unsecured exchangeable notes with an embedded exchange option and capped call. Parties: PBF Holding and PBF Finance as issuers, PBF Energy Inc. as a party to the indenture and registration rights agreement, U.S. Bank Trust Company as trustee. Status: completed 2026-09-17. Amount: 550.0; net proceeds about 533.2, of which 27.7 paid for the capped call and the rest, with cash, redeemed the 2030 7.875% notes (Q3-10Q page:18 "The Issuers used $27.7 million of the net proceeds to pay the cost of the capped call transactions"). Terms: no regular interest and no principal accretion (Q3-10Q page:18 "The 2032 Exchangeable Notes do not bear regular interest, and the principal amount of the 2032 Exchangeable Notes will not accrete."), maturity 2032-01-15, initial exchange rate of 10.3306 PBF Energy Class A shares per 1,000 of principal (Q3-10Q page:18 "initial exchange rate is 10.3306 shares of PBF Energy Class A common stock, per $1,000 principal amount"), exchange price about $96.80, capped call cap price about $123.20 (Q3-10Q page:21 "initial cap price of approximately $123.20 per share"), settlement in cash up to principal with the excess in cash or PBF Energy shares at the issuers' election (Q3-10Q page:18 "will be settled in cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the notes being exchanged"). Mechanics: the exchange feature is a bifurcated derivative liability that the issuer marks to fair value, at 197.6 at 2026-09-30 with a 29.9 unrealized loss in Q3 2026, using a PBF Energy share price input of $76.96 (Q3-10Q page:31 "Share price $ 76.96"); the debt host carries a large discount with an effective rate of about 7.0%. Creditor implication: zero cash coupon lowers cash interest, but the issuer carries the principal in cash settlement, the derivative creates earnings volatility linked to the parent's share price, and the instrument depends on parent equity; Analyst Interpretation. A registration rights agreement requires PBF Energy to file a shelf by 2026-12-31 with special interest of 0.25% rising to 0.50% if the issuers fail to comply (Q3-10Q page:20 "on or prior to December 31, 2026").

Redemptions. 2030 7.875% notes: 500.0 redeemed 2026-09-24 at 103.938%, about 519.7 (Q3-10Q page:21 "redeemed at a price equal to 103.938% of the aggregate principal amount thereof"). 2028 6.00% notes: 801.6 redeemed 2026-06-25 at 100%. 2030 9.875% notes: 800.0 redeemed 2026-10-26 at 106.67%, about 853.4, from cash on hand; this is a Subsequent event, with a loss on extinguishment of 70.4 to be booked in Q4 2026 (Q3-10Q page:33 "will be recorded as a Loss on extinguishment of debt in the Consolidated Statements of Operations in the fourth quarter of 2026"). Liquidity effect: cash on hand funds the redemption, reducing cash by about 853.4 plus accrued interest from the 2,510.6 at 2026-09-30. Each redemption was a full redemption of the series, so no holder was treated differently within a series (Analyst Interpretation); no priming, uptier, drop-down or non-pro-rata exchange is documented.

Asset-based revolving credit facility. Type: amendment and restatement of the 2023 agreement with Bank of America as administrative agent. Status: effective 2026-09-30 (Q3-10Q page:24 "extended the Revolving Credit Facility through September 30, 2031, increased the maximum commitment from $3.5 billion to $4.0 billion, and reduced the commitment fees on the unused portion"). It was drawn 100.0 at 2025-12-31 and 750.0 at 2026-03-31, and undrawn at 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30 (financial base handoff). Security: the 10-K describes liens on the parent's equity in the issuer and on receivables, inventory and deposit accounts (10K page:181 "secured by a lien on (i) PBF LLC"), which ranks the revolver ahead of the unsecured notes to the extent of collateral. Executed agreement not supplied.

Hydrogen plants asset purchase. Type: purchase of two hydrogen plants at the Torrance refinery previously under operating leases. Parties: PBF LLC and Air Products; contributed to the issuer. Status: closed 2026-09-09. Issuer accounting: property of about 388.4 recognised, lease liability of 139.7 and right-of-use asset of 140.2 derecognised (Q3-10Q page:13 "PBF LLC contributed the hydrogen production plants to the Company"). The Q2 10-Q described the agreement differently: the issuer "will become the owner and operator", with "a secured promissory note to be issued by PBF LLC" valued at an estimated 320.0 to 340.0 (Q2-10Q page:26 "The transaction includes a secured promissory note to be issued by PBF LLC that will become effective upon closing"). The Q3 10-Q does not mention the note, the security for it or any issuer guarantee. Status of consideration and any lien on the plants: Insufficient Information. This is logged as a conflict below. Creditor implication: operating lease obligations fell, but a secured parent-level note linked to assets now in the issuer's group could affect collateral and restricted-payment capacity if the security touches issuer assets; the pack cannot confirm either way.

Distributions and the parent dividend. Type: recurring distributions to the parent chain. The issuer states it may need to distribute cash to PBF LLC for the parent's dividend of $0.325 per share declared 2026-10-29 and payable 2026-11-24 (Q3-10Q page:33 "The Company may need to make cash distributions to PBF LLC to the extent necessary for PBF Energy to pay this dividend."). Subsequent event; the amount to be distributed by the issuer is not stated.

Martinez refinery fire and insurance. Status: the refinery returned to full operations in May 2026; cumulative insurance proceeds of 1.25 billion net of deductibles (Q3-10Q page:15 "has received cumulative insurance proceeds, net of deductibles and retentions, of $1.25 billion"); investigations by regulators continue and potential liabilities are unknown. Management expects to finalize the insurance claim process before year-end 2026 (Q3-PR page:2 "Working with our insurance group, PBF expects to finalize the claim process before year-end 2026."), a Management Language claim at the parent perimeter.

Chalmette refinery fire. A fire on 2026-05-08 is named among risk factors (Q3-10Q page:5 "the fire on May 8, 2026 at our Chalmette refinery"); no amount, repair timeline or insurance position was found in any pinned source after searching "May 8" and "Chalmette" with fire, outage and incident. Insufficient Information.

fields.value: The issuer's financial base is the filed statements of PBF Holding Company LLC. They show a sharp turn from a trough to a strong position within three quarters. FY2025 was a loss year: a net loss of 481.3, income from operations of -292.6 even after an 832.5 gain on insurance recoveries, and company-defined Adjusted EBITDA of only 29.5 (10K page:123 "Adjusted EBITDA $ 29.5 $ (79.9) $ 2,408.0"). In the first nine months of 2026 net income was 3,269.6 and Adjusted EBITDA was 3,284.3 (Q3-10Q page:59 "Adjusted EBITDA $ 2,139.3 $ 91.5 $ 3,284.3 $ (191.4)"). Management attributes the increase to crack spreads and crude differentials affected by geopolitical conflict and to higher throughput after the Martinez restart (Q3-10Q page:43 "a significant increase in refining margins"); this is management language and is not adopted as a forecast. Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 supply 3,278.6 of the 3,505.2 LTM Adjusted EBITDA, so the trailing figure is exposed to whether those margins persist. Debt was reorganised during 2026: the 2028 6.00% and 2030 7.875% notes were redeemed, 500.0 of 2034 7.25% notes and 550.0 of 2032 exchangeable notes were issued, and the revolver was amended and extended; at 30 September 2026 principal debt was 1,850.0 against cash of 2,510.6, and on 26 October 2026, after the period, the 800.0 of 2030 9.875% notes were redeemed using cash on hand. Leverage on company Adjusted EBITDA is therefore distorted at both ends of the series: not meaningful at FY2024 and FY2025 because EBITDA is negative or near zero, and very low at LTM Q3 2026. Interest cover uses cash interest paid net of capitalised interest and so overstates cover relative to total interest. Debt is only part of the claim stack: lease, pension, purchase, environmental, emissions and legal claims sit outside it and are set out below. Liquidity is printed as rounded narrative amounts whose build cannot be reproduced from the pack. Perimeter discipline matters: the parent's releases print different cash, debt and operating income, and none of them is used for an issuer figure. This view is a financial extraction and a structured set of limitations; it is not a credit rating, a recommendation or a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer, PBF Holding Company LLC, is the borrowing and operating holding company for six U.S. refineries with about 1,000,000 barrels per day of capacity, reported as one segment, and it is wholly owned by PBF Energy Company LLC under the listed parent PBF Energy Inc. Its revenue is the sale of unbranded fuels and other refined products at prevailing market prices, almost 89% of it gasoline and distillates, to a diverse base with one customer, Shell, at about 13% of revenue. Because crude and product prices both float, the business has little pricing control: results depend on industry crack spreads, crude differentials, throughput, refinery reliability and the cost of renewable fuel credits. That mechanism explains the swing from a loss year in FY2025, when the Martinez refinery was shut and then restarting, to very large earnings in 2026, when management says geopolitical conflict widened margins and the Martinez refinery returned to full operations in May 2026. The creditor reading is that the operating model is cyclical and event-exposed, with the business risk concentrated in refinery uptime, margin volatility, environmental and emissions obligations and legal investigations, rather than in customer or contract concentration. The transaction picture in 2026 is a refinancing and simplification: the 6.00% notes due 2028 and the 7.875% notes due 2030 were redeemed, 500.0 of 7.25% notes due 2034 and 550.0 of zero-coupon exchangeable notes due 2032 were issued, the asset-based revolver was amended to a 4,000.0 commitment through 2031-09-30, and after the quarter the 9.875% notes due 2030 were redeemed on 2026-10-26 with cash on hand. The new exchangeable notes are exchangeable into shares of the parent, which links the issuer's liabilities and reported earnings to the parent's share price. Ownership is a listed-parent structure with no financial sponsor named in the pack, and documented behaviour toward creditors is mixed: parent cash contributions and full-par or premium note redemptions are supportive, while distributions to the parent chain to fund its dividends, past asset distributions to affiliates and the parent-level secured note on the hydrogen plants are items a creditor should track. This is a fact pack, not a rating or a recommendation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2034 7.25% senior notes. Type: new senior unsecured notes. Parties: PBF Holding and PBF Finance as issuers with certain subsidiary guarantors, Wilmington Trust as trustee. Status: completed 2026-05-28 (Q3-10Q page:21 "the Issuers issued $500.0 million in aggregate principal amount of 2034 7.25% Senior Notes"). Use of proceeds: net proceeds of 492.1 plus available cash redeemed all of the 2028 6.00% notes on 2026-06-25 (Q3-10Q page:23 "On June 25, 2026, the Company redeemed all $801.6 million aggregate principal amount outstanding of its 2028 6.00% Senior Notes"). Terms: guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis, effectively subordinated to secured debt including the revolver, structurally subordinated to non-guarantor subsidiaries, with a change-of-control repurchase at 101% on a ratings decline (Q3-10Q page:23 "at a purchase price of 101% of the principal amount"). Liquidity effect: cash used was the shortfall between the notes redeemed and net proceeds, and the 2028 maturity was removed. Creditor implication: the nearest maturity moved from 2028 to 2034 for this tranche, at a higher coupon than the notes replaced but with maturity extension; Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2032 0.00% exchangeable senior notes. Type: new senior unsecured exchangeable notes with an embedded exchange option and capped call. Parties: PBF Holding and PBF Finance as issuers, PBF Energy Inc. as a party to the indenture and registration rights agreement, U.S. Bank Trust Company as trustee. Status: completed 2026-09-17. Amount: 550.0; net proceeds about 533.2, of which 27.7 paid for the capped call and the rest, with cash, redeemed the 2030 7.875% notes (Q3-10Q page:18 "The Issuers used $27.7 million of the net proceeds to pay the cost of the capped call transactions"). Terms: no regular interest and no principal accretion (Q3-10Q page:18 "The 2032 Exchangeable Notes do not bear regular interest, and the principal amount of the 2032 Exchangeable Notes will not accrete."), maturity 2032-01-15, initial exchange rate of 10.3306 PBF Energy Class A shares per 1,000 of principal (Q3-10Q page:18 "initial exchange rate is 10.3306 shares of PBF Energy Class A common stock, per $1,000 principal amount"), exchange price about $96.80, capped call cap price about $123.20 (Q3-10Q page:21 "initial cap price of approximately $123.20 per share"), settlement in cash up to principal with the excess in cash or PBF Energy shares at the issuers' election (Q3-10Q page:18 "will be settled in cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the notes being exchanged"). Mechanics: the exchange feature is a bifurcated derivative liability that the issuer marks to fair value, at 197.6 at 2026-09-30 with a 29.9 unrealized loss in Q3 2026, using a PBF Energy share price input of $76.96 (Q3-10Q page:31 "Share price $ 76.96"); the debt host carries a large discount with an effective rate of about 7.0%. Creditor implication: zero cash coupon lowers cash interest, but the issuer carries the principal in cash settlement, the derivative creates earnings volatility linked to the parent's share price, and the instrument depends on parent equity; Analyst Interpretation. A registration rights agreement requires PBF Energy to file a shelf by 2026-12-31 with special interest of 0.25% rising to 0.50% if the issuers fail to comply (Q3-10Q page:20 "on or prior to December 31, 2026").

Liquidity effect: cash on hand funds the redemption, reducing cash by about 853.4 plus accrued interest from the 2,510.6 at 2026-09-30. Each redemption was a full redemption of the series, so no holder was treated differently within a series (Analyst Interpretation); no priming, uptier, drop-down or non-pro-rata exchange is documented.

fields.value: Asset-based revolving credit facility. Type: amendment and restatement of the 2023 agreement with Bank of America as administrative agent. Status: effective 2026-09-30 (Q3-10Q page:24 "extended the Revolving Credit Facility through September 30, 2031, increased the maximum commitment from $3.5 billion to $4.0 billion, and reduced the commitment fees on the unused portion"). It was drawn 100.0 at 2025-12-31 and 750.0 at 2026-03-31, and undrawn at 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30 (financial base handoff). fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hydrogen plants asset purchase. Type: purchase of two hydrogen plants at the Torrance refinery previously under operating leases. Parties: PBF LLC and Air Products; contributed to the issuer. Status: closed 2026-09-09. Issuer accounting: property of about 388.4 recognised, lease liability of 139.7 and right-of-use asset of 140.2 derecognised (Q3-10Q page:13 "PBF LLC contributed the hydrogen production plants to the Company"). The Q2 10-Q described the agreement differently: the issuer "will become the owner and operator", with "a secured promissory note to be issued by PBF LLC" valued at an estimated 320.0 to 340.0 (Q2-10Q page:26 "The transaction includes a secured promissory note to be issued by PBF LLC that will become effective upon closing"). The Q3 10-Q does not mention the note, the security for it or any issuer guarantee. Status of consideration and any lien on the plants: Insufficient Information. This is logged as a conflict below. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Revenue durability and margin risk. Evidence: revenues are priced at spot market (Q3-10Q page:28 "These revenues are largely based on the current spot (market) prices of the products sold") and the Q3 2026 margin rise is attributed by management to crack spreads and differentials (Q3-10Q page:45 "Average industry margins were notably more favorable"). Risk mechanic: no price floor and no contractual margin, so cash flow tracks external spreads and refinery uptime. Credit implication: debt service capacity is high when spreads are wide and thin when they narrow, as FY2025 showed with Adjusted EBITDA of 29.5; the trailing LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 3,505.2 rests on two quarters. Counter-evidence logged: management says refining fundamentals remained exceptionally strong (Q3-PR page:1 "refining fundamentals remained exceptionally strong"), Management Language not adopted as a forecast. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Refinancing and liquidity. Evidence: the 2026 notes sequence, the revolver extension to 2031-09-30 and cash of 2,510.6 at 2026-09-30 with 800.0 redeemed afterwards. Risk mechanic: removal of 2028 and 2030 maturities and the zero-coupon exchangeable lowers refinancing and interest burden; the secured revolver ranks ahead of unsecured notes in collateral. Credit implication: refinancing risk is low in the near term for this perimeter; effective subordination of the unsecured notes to the revolver and to the parent-linked exchange feature should be monitored. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Concentration. Evidence: Shell at about 13% of revenue, six refineries across four regions. Risk mechanic: customer concentration is modest; asset concentration is in the Martinez and Torrance West Coast refineries and regulatory exposure in California. Credit implication: event risk at one refinery (as the Martinez fire showed) matters more than customer loss. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Sponsor alignment and leakage. Evidence: distributions to the parent chain, asset distributions to PBFX and SBR, parent dividend funding language, hydrogen contribution. Risk mechanic: cash can move up to fund parent dividends when liquidity is strong; restricted payment covenants are not supplied. Credit implication: Neutral or Mixed; monitor distributions against liquidity and the hydrogen note security. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

fields.value: 5. Key uncertainties. Evidence: unquantified Martinez investigations, the Chalmette fire, the hydrogen note, labour agreements and the missing documents. Credit implication: open items could add cash costs or lien constraints; they are information gaps, not adverse conclusions.

fields.value: PBF Holding Company LLC has a sound credit profile at 30 September 2026 that has not yet been tested through a normal-margin year. Its strongest support is liquidity and leverage: USD 2,510.6 million of cash against USD 1,850.0 million of debt principal, net cash of USD 660.6 million, and a USD 4,000.0 million revolver running to 30 September 2031. fields.value: First, the issuer's balance sheet is strong at the latest reported date. Principal debt was USD 1,850.0 million against cash of USD 2,510.6 million, giving net cash of USD 660.6 million and leverage of 0.5x total debt and -0.2x net debt on twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 3,505.2 million [CP-1 net debt and leverage calculation]. After the redemption of USD 800.0 million of 9.875% notes on 26 October 2026 for about USD 853.4 million, principal falls to USD 1,050.0 million and cash to roughly USD 1,657.2 million before accrued interest and other flows, which is an illustration and not a reported balance [CP-1 illustrative effects]. Category: Documentary Fact for the reported figures, Analyst Interpretation for the illustration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, the issuer's earnings swung from a trough to very high levels, and the trailing figure is concentrated. Adjusted EBITDA was USD 29.5 million in FY2025, USD 1,139.3 million in Q2 2026 and USD 2,139.3 million in Q3 2026 [CP-1 financials table]. The business is priced at spot market and has no contractual margin protection, so the issuer's debt capacity follows crack spreads, crude differentials, throughput and compliance costs [CP-1A operating model]. Management attributes the 2026 strength to conflict-driven market conditions and describes them as uncertain in duration; that is Management Language and is not adopted as a forecast. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, the issuer's refinancing in 2026 removed near-term maturities and lowered stated coupon cost. The 6.00% notes due 2028 and 7.875% notes due 2030 were redeemed, USD 500.0 million of 7.25% notes due 2034 and USD 550.0 million of zero-coupon exchangeable notes due 2032 were issued, and the secured revolver was extended with a USD 4,000.0 million commitment [CP-1A transaction summary]. Stated coupons retired of about USD 166.5 million a year compare with about USD 36.3 million on the new fixed notes, excluding revolver fees and discount amortisation. The exchangeable notes settle principal in cash and are linked to the parent's share price, creating a fair-value liability of USD 197.6 million that moves earnings [CP-1 debt instruments; CP-1A transaction summary]. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, claims outside the reported debt are material. They include operating lease liabilities of USD 712.3 million at 30 September 2026, pension and post-retirement medical deficits of USD 89.8 million and USD 16.4 million at 31 December 2025, fixed purchase commitments of USD 642.9 million, renewable energy credit and emissions obligations of USD 486.5 million and environmental liabilities of USD 148.4 million, plus unquantified investigations into the Martinez fire and catalyst release [CP-1 claims outside the debt figure]. These rank alongside debt in a downside case and are not in the leverage ratios. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, the issuer's cash flows with its parent were supportive in the downturn and have turned outward as earnings recovered. Parent contributions exceeded distributions by USD 199.6 million in FY2025, but in Q3 2026 distributions exceeded contributions by USD 60.9 million, and the issuer may distribute cash to fund the parent's dividend [CP-1A ownership and behaviour]. Documented behaviour toward creditors is Neutral or Mixed: full redemptions at par or a premium and transparent reporting are supportive, while past asset distributions to affiliates and the parent-level secured note on the hydrogen plants are open. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, the evidence has gaps that limit how far the view can be pushed: no forecast or through-the-cycle earnings case, no executed indentures or credit agreement, a liquidity figure that cannot be rebuilt, and an unexplained difference between issuer and parent debt figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. The issuer has low reported leverage and net cash: 0.5x total debt and -0.2x net debt to twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, and cash interest paid of USD 162.3 million against Adjusted EBITDA of USD 3,505.2 million, or 21.6x cover on a measure that excludes capitalised interest [CP-1 interest cover]. Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading. The issuer has liquidity depth, with USD 2,510.6 million of cash and about USD 3,100.0 million of rounded borrowing availability, and no revolver drawing at the quarter end [CP-1 liquidity]. Its maturity profile has no drawn debt maturing before 2032 after the October redemption [CP-1 debt maturities]. Its asset base is diversified across six refineries in four regions with one customer at about 13% of revenue, so customer loss is a smaller risk than a single refinery event [CP-1A operating model]. The parent supported the issuer with net contributions of USD 199.6 million in the FY2025 downturn and contributed the hydrogen plants in Q3 2026 [CP-1A ownership and behaviour].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. The issuer's earnings depend on external margins and uptime: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 29.5 million in FY2025 against USD 3,505.2 million over the latest twelve months, with USD 3,278.6 million from two quarters. Analyst Interpretation resting on the CP-1 figures. The issuer faces event risk at single sites: the Martinez fire investigations and the 8 May 2026 Chalmette fire have no quantified impact [CP-1A transaction summary]. Cash can leave to the parent chain and the exchangeable notes link the issuer to the parent's share price, with a fair-value liability of USD 197.6 million [CP-1A behaviour table; CP-1 debt instruments]. Large claims sit outside debt, notably leases, purchase commitments, emissions credits and environmental liabilities [CP-1 claims outside debt]. The revolver is secured and ranks ahead of the unsecured notes to the extent of its collateral; the unsecured notes are also structurally behind non-guarantor subsidiaries, a structural mechanic and not a recovery conclusion [CP-1 debt instruments]. Regulatory compliance cost is large and volatile: renewable fuel compliance cost was USD 522.8 million in Q3 2026 against USD 169.0 million a year earlier [CP-1A operating model].
